thread:
david: Heads up — ZenBank asked for an SLO proposal. They're pushing for p95=150ms, p99=350ms at our standard hosted tier. I want to align on whether that's feasible without dedicated capacity.

leo: p95=150 is probably ok for short prompts on 1B-3B-class models w/ aggressive kernels and microbatch=2. p99=350 is tight because KV warmups + cold KV cache tail shows 3-4x p95.

maria: can you share the latest profile? did the KV prefill patch land on prod?

leo: attaching quick paste from profiler (sampled on canary):
```
profile: run=2026-02-12T14:22Z
model: redwood-3b-quant
microbatch: 4
p50: 45ms
p95: 172ms
p99: 412ms
kv_hit_rate: 0.62
cold_kv95: 520ms
kernel_swap: 2.4ms
```

leo: notes: p95 around 170 with microbatch=4, but p99 spikes when KV misses + large seq lengths. Kernel swap overhead negligible.

sam: @david @leo ZenBank's product team said 95th must be under 200ms for interactive UI. Sales also asked for a guaranteed p99 target. Tara, what flexibility do they have?

tara: they want a single SLA for both desktop and mobile. their legal team prefers p99 <= 500ms during steady QPS (~400 rps). They can pay for dedicated but prefer hosted if cheaper.

maria: clarification — "steady" vs "peak"? what's their burst profile? cold starts?

tara: steady ~400 rps, spikes up to 1k for 3-5 min during batch events. They want no more than 2 outages / month.

leo: options:
- Option A (hosted): microbatch=2, aggressive kernel + prefix cache TTL=24h, offer p95<=200ms, p99 best-effort ~500ms with carveouts for cache-cold tails.
- Option B (hosted + reserved burst): same as A but reserve burst nodes + KV prefill job => p99 ~350-400ms.
- Option C (dedicated): pin capacity, pre-warmed KV, p95<=150, p99<=300 guaranteed.

maria: highlight risk: KV cold-miss tail is correlated with user QPS distribution. If we don't prefill, p99 tail will exceed 500ms during cache churn.

sam: product ask: can we offer a tiered SLA text like "p95 150ms; p99 350ms during steady-state (>=10m running) else p99 500ms"? that lets us avoid promising cold-start behavior.

david: that seems reasonable. also propose: provide a migration plan to Dedicated if they opt-in after 30 days of traffic. Sales gets a clear escalation.

leo: quick microbench notes i ran tonight (local sim):
```
config A: microbatch=2, kv_prefill=true -> p95 138ms, p99 312ms at 450 rps
config B: microbatch=8, kv_prefill=false -> p95 160ms, p99 620ms at 450 rps
```

leo: takeaway: smaller microbatch reduces p99 but increases GPU overhead / cost. With prefill, p99 improves ~40%.

tara: pricing question — can we estimate delta cost for prefill + reserved burst? need numbers for the commercial offer.

maria: I'll run a quick cost calc: prefill adds ~0.5-1 GPU-hour/day depending on model, reserved burst nodes priced as +20% of baseline. I'll post numbers by EOD.

ci-bot: profile-job #472 completed: canary -> prod diff: p99 regressions observed for routes: /chat/stream when KV_hit_rate < 0.7. See /ci/artifacts/472/logs.

leo: thanks CI bot — I'll dig into the route traces. If we can bump KV hit rate via smarter prefix caching or localized prefill, we can close most of the p99 gap.

sam: one more ask from product: include a short explainer for ZenBank legal about "what p99 covers" and the carveouts (cache-cold windows, forceful network degradation, etc.). I'll draft the wording after we decide numbers.

david: action items:
- leo: validate microbatch=2 can sustain 400 rps with acceptable cost and run extended 1hr sim.
- maria: cost delta for prefill + reserved burst by EOD.
- sam/tara: draft SLA proposal with carveouts and migration path.

tara: sounds good — I'll flag this as high priority for the deal. :thumbsup:

leo: I'll start the sim now, will post results in the thread when done.
